Load when creating stateful agents, durable workflows, real-time WebSocket apps, scheduled tasks, MCP servers, chat applications, voice agents, or browser automation. Use when building stateful coordination (chat rooms, multiplayer games, booking systems), implementing RPC methods, SQLite storage, alarms, WebSockets, or reviewing DO code for best practices. - design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. # Build plan

The plan for taking cache-ttl-analyzer from scaffolding to a deployed MVP.
Grounded in the research at
[docs/design/claude-code-session-logs/feasibility.md](design/claude-code-session-logs/feasibility.md)
(referenced below as "the feasibility doc") — read it before implementing the
parser or simulator; it documents the traps that make naive implementations
silently wrong.

This plan is decomposed into **work packages (WPs)** sized for individual Claude
sessions, with an explicit dependency graph so independent WPs can run in
parallel.

---

## 1. MVP definition

A static web app, deployed to Cloudflare, where a user:

1. Uploads **one Claude Code session log (JSONL)** at a time — or loads a
   bundled sample.
2. Watches analysis run **entirely in their browser** (Web Worker), with a
   progress indicator and a cancel button.
3. Gets a verdict: what the session actually cost at published Anthropic API
   rates, what it *would have cost* under the other cache TTL (5m vs 1h), and a
   recommendation.
4. Sees cache-behavior insights: cache invalidations (expiry gaps, and hard
   resets from model / effort / version changes), warm-read counts, and short
   educational explanations of each.
5. Can revisit sessions analyzed earlier in the same browser session
   (in-memory history only — nothing persisted).

Plus: clear instructions for finding session logs on macOS and Windows, a
prominent privacy statement ("analysis is local; this is open source — verify
it yourself" with a link to the repo), a dedicated **data policy page** (see
§3a), and a "prices as of" date on every dollar figure.

Two cross-cutting requirements, cheap now and expensive to retrofit:

- **Localization-ready from day one.** MVP ships English only, but no
  user-facing string is hard-coded in a component: all copy lives in locale
  resource files (react-i18next or equivalent — chosen in WP-07), and all
  number, currency, date, and duration formatting goes through the `Intl`
  APIs keyed to the active locale. Adding a second language later must be a
  translation task, not a refactor.
- **Data policy page**: a first-class page, linked from the footer and the
  upload screen, stating in plain language: analysis runs entirely in the
  browser; the file is never uploaded, stored, or sent anywhere; the strict
  CSP enforces this at the platform level (with a one-line "check devtools"
  pointer); no analytics or tracking in the MVP; the project is open source
  (repo link); and any future optional API-powered analysis will be opt-in
  with an explicit, itemized disclosure of what would be sent.

### Non-goals for MVP (deferred, in rough priority order)

- **Anthropic API deep-analysis feature** (upload timestamps/token counts for
  richer analysis). Deferred until MVP proves useful. When picked up, the
  BYO-API-key vs. our-key-plus-rate-limiting decision gets made then.
- Multi-file / folder upload and cross-session rollups (requires global dedup
  and cross-session cache modeling — feasibility doc §6.3, §7).
- Provider-specific rate tables (Bedrock, Vertex). MVP uses Anthropic
  published API rates only — see decision log.
- Claude Code **web JSON export** input. Unverified that it carries `usage`
  (feasibility doc §10). JSONL only for MVP.
- Durable persistence, accounts, authentication.
- In-app billing-mode questionnaire (feasibility §3 suggests asking the user;
  MVP states the API-rates framing as a label instead — see D12).
- Hybrid-TTL guidance (1h stable prefix + 5m tail, feasibility §10) — the
  logs can't support a computed number, only qualitative advice; revisit
  post-MVP.

---

## 2. Architecture

- **Stack:** React + TypeScript + Vite. Deployed as **static assets on
  Cloudflare Workers** via Wrangler. **No server-side code in the MVP** — this
  is deliberate: the strongest form of the privacy claim is that there is no
  backend to send data to.
- **Analysis engine** (`src/engine/`): pure TypeScript, zero DOM/React
  dependencies, so it runs in a Web Worker and is unit-testable in Node.
  - **Parser** reads only the fields it needs (`type`, `timestamp`,
    `message.id`, `message.model`, `message.usage`, `isSidechain`, `agentId`,
    `effort`, `version`, plus `uuid`/`parentUuid`/`timestamp` of `user` and
    `attachment` rows for threading and request-start pairing, and
    `sessionId`/`cwd`/`gitBranch` for the identification card) and **never
    reads `message.content`** — enforced by a test that
    feeds a session whose content blocks are poison values and asserts they
    never appear in any output (feasibility doc §9). One deliberate, named
    exception: the `ai-title` record (the short session title Claude Code
    generates), read for the session identification card (§3) — a single
    string, not conversation content. Not every session has one (4 of 7 in
    the research corpus); payload shape to be verified in WP-03.
  - **Simulator** implements the counterfactual model from the feasibility
    doc: see §3 below.
- **Web Worker** wraps the engine: streams the file
  (`File.stream()` + line splitting, so large logs don't need one giant
  string), posts progress messages, and supports cancellation (terminate).
- **Pricing config** (`src/config/pricing.json`): per-model base rates, cache
  multipliers (read 0.1×, 5m write 1.25×, 1h write 2.0×), `service_tier` and
  `speed` modifiers, and a top-level `pricesAsOf` date shown in the UI.
  Unknown model IDs are reported to the user, never guessed; degradation
  policy: unpriced requests are excluded and disclosed, their share measured
  in **total tokens (input + cache + output) across deduped requests**, and
  the verdict is suppressed when that share exceeds **10%** (both the metric
  and the constant are named in the WP-02 contract so verdicts are
  deterministic).
- **UI** consumes a frozen engine contract (WP-02) so UI and engine work can
  proceed in parallel.
- **Logging** goes through a small leveled abstraction (`loglevel`, `tslog`,
  or a thin wrapper — chosen in WP-01), used everywhere including the worker
  (worker log events forwarded to the main thread). Quiet by default in
  production; a debug flag (query param or `localStorage` toggle, documented
  on the data policy page) elevates verbosity so users can self-serve
  troubleshooting output. **Console-only, never shipped anywhere** — remote
  log collection would contradict the CSP/privacy stance. Anything the user
  needs to act on (skipped records, warnings) still surfaces in the UI, not
  just the log.

### Input validation and secure file handling

The app is static and client-side, so the threat model is a malicious or
corrupted **file** being processed in the user's own browser — plus proving to
users that nothing is exfiltrated. Rules:

- **Three validation verdicts:** *valid*; *valid with warnings* (skipped
  records, out-of-range version, unknown model); or *not a session log* — no
  assistant rows carrying `usage`, or malformed lines exceeding **10% of
  non-empty lines** (an exact named constant in the WP-02 contract) — with a
  plain-language error, never a garbage analysis.
- **Numeric hygiene:** every usage field is checked finite and non-negative
  before pricing; bad rows are skipped and counted.
- **Log-derived strings are untrusted input.** Title, `cwd`, `gitBranch`,
  model IDs render only as text nodes (no `innerHTML` anywhere), length-clamped.
- **No raw JSON into app state.** The parser copies the needed fields into
  typed records and discards the parsed object — no spreading of parsed
  objects, which also neutralizes prototype-pollution keys (`__proto__`,
  `constructor`).
- **Resource limits:** file-size cap with a clear message; streaming parse
  with a per-line length cap so one giant line can't exhaust tab memory;
  analysis in a worker so the page stays responsive; cancel always available.
- **CSP as proof, not just promise:** deploy with a strict
  Content-Security-Policy (`default-src 'self'`; no external `connect-src`)
  so "your data never leaves the browser" is enforced by the platform and
  verifiable in devtools — and mention that in the privacy statement.
- **Nothing persisted:** the file is never written to storage; in-memory
  history keeps analysis results, not file bytes.

### Engine correctness rules (from the feasibility doc — all mandatory)

| Rule | Source |
|---|---|
| Dedup rows on `message.id` (one row per content block, each carries full usage; up to 13× overstatement otherwise) | §6.1 |
| Exclude `message.model == "<synthetic>"` rows | §6.2 |
| Partition sidechains **per subagent thread**, not as one boolean bucket: each subagent has its own cache namespace. **Amended by the WP-02 inspection (2026-08-30, contract F2):** on v2.1.251 subagent transcripts are *separate files* (`<project>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-<agentId>.jsonl`, rows carrying `agentId` and `isSidechain: true`, `parentUuid` chains self-contained) — not interleaved rows in the main file, which is a legacy-version case. Thread key = `agentId` when present; otherwise the row belongs to the main thread unless `isSidechain` is true, in which case threads are recovered from `parentUuid`-chain roots. Consequence: a modern main-session upload contains **no** subagent traffic; the subagent bucket appears when the uploaded file is itself a subagent transcript or a legacy interleaved log | §6.4 + review + WP-02 inspection |
| Hard cache reset on any change of `model`, `effort`, or `version`, independent of elapsed time | §6.6 |
| Price per request (models/tiers/speed can vary mid-session); honor `service_tier` and `speed` | §6.5 |
| Gap timing: request start = the nearest `user`-row ancestor's timestamp found by walking `parentUuid` (**refined by the WP-02 inspection, contract F3:** the immediate parent is usually an `attachment` row, so the walk must index `uuid`/`parentUuid`/`timestamp` of `user` *and* `attachment` rows — metadata only, never content); fall back to the assistant row's own timestamp when no ancestor resolves | §7 + review + WP-02 inspection |
| Expiry model is all-or-nothing per gap; this is conservative toward 5m — disclose it in the UI | §7 |
| Effective TTL comes from `usage.cache_creation` (`ephemeral_5m` / `ephemeral_1h` split). Counterfactuals reprice **only the user-controllable share**; server-tool 5m writes stay at 5m in both scenarios and are tracked as their own expiry class. The reconciliation check (§5) replays each request with its **observed per-request split**, not a single session-wide TTL | §2 + review |
| Unrecognized record types are skipped and counted, surfaced as "N records skipped" | §4 |
| Warn (don't fail) when `version` is outside the validated range | §4 |

---

## 3. What the analysis reports

**First, a session identification card** so the user can confirm they loaded
the session they intended — built entirely from content-free metadata: the
session title (from the `ai-title` record when present), working directory
(`cwd`), git branch, date and time span, duration, request count, model(s),
Claude Code version, and file name/size. Message content is never shown; the
card is why it never needs to be.

**Headline:** the main-conversation bucket. Cost at 5m vs cost at 1h,
recommendation, and delta — labelled as *notional cost at published Anthropic
API rates* with a one-line rationale (subscription users have no per-token
bill; API-rate framing is what an API/Bedrock/credits user pays and what
everyone should understand — see decision log).

**Conditionally:** if the uploaded file contains sidechain turns — a legacy
log with interleaved `isSidechain` rows, or a modern per-subagent transcript
from `<session-id>/subagents/` uploaded directly (WP-02 inspection, contract
F2) — a second section
for the **subagent bucket** (`subagentPromptCacheTtl`), with its own
recommendation. When no sidechains exist, this section does not appear, and
the tool does not imply it evaluated subagent traffic (feasibility doc §3).

**Insights (the educational layer):**

- Timeline of cache events: writes, warm reads, expiries (with the gap that
  caused each), hard resets (annotated with the cause: model switch, effort
  change, version upgrade).
- Counts: cache invalidations, warm-read requests, wasted-write tokens.
- Observed effective TTL per bucket, and whether the configuration was
  provably explicit (the two unambiguous patterns from feasibility doc §3) —
  otherwise no claim about defaults.
- Session shape summary: request count, span, largest gap, share of gaps in
  the 5m–1h band (the only band where the choice matters).
- A pointer to Claude Code's built-in live cache stats (`/usage`, v2.1.251+)
  for monitoring cache behavior going forward.

---

## 4. Work packages

Sized so each WP is one focused session producing one PR into `main`. Every PR
passes CI (typecheck, lint, tests, build) and CodeRabbit review.

### WP-01 — Scaffold and tooling ✅ complete (PR #11, 2026-08-30)
**Depends on:** nothing. **Blocks:** everything.
Vite + React + TS app skeleton; Vitest; Oxlint + Prettier (D14 — was
"ESLint + Prettier"); `wrangler.jsonc`
for Workers static assets; npm scripts (`dev`, `build`, `test`, `lint`,
`typecheck`, `deploy`); the logging abstraction (an in-house ~100-line
wrapper was chosen, `src/lib/logger.ts`) with the debug-flag mechanism;
README "Development" section filled in.
*Acceptance:* `npm run build && npm test` green; `wrangler dev` serves the
placeholder app.

### WP-02 — Engine contract (do in the same session as WP-01) ✅ complete (PR #11, 2026-08-30)
**Depends on:** WP-01. **Blocks:** WP-03, WP-04, WP-05, WP-07, WP-08.
The frozen TypeScript interfaces everything else codes against:
`ParsedSession` (deduped request records + skip/warning counts),
`AnalysisResult` (per-bucket actual/counterfactual costs, recommendation,
insight events), the Web Worker message protocol (start / progress / cancel /
result / error), and the `pricing.json` schema.

**Before freezing, inspect real session logs** to resolve the known unknowns
that would otherwise force amendments: the `ai-title` payload shape, the
user-row → assistant-row request-start pairing, and sidechain thread
identification (`parentUuid`/`uuid` chains) against a real multi-subagent
session. The contract must also pin down two semantics the analysis depends
on: the **unknown-model degradation policy** (excluded-and-disclosed;
verdict suppressed above a threshold) and **mixed-TTL write handling** in
counterfactuals (server tools insert their own 5m writes regardless of the
user's setting — default model: hold them at 5m in both scenarios as a
separate expiry class and reprice only the user-controllable share; WP-02
finalizes and documents this so the simulator is deterministic).

Documented inline; changes after freeze require touching this plan. The
insight-event taxonomy is the one section expected to be amended (WP-08 and
WP-D consume it and will discover needs).

**Inspection outcome (2026-08-30):** findings F1–F7 are recorded at the top
of `src/engine/contract.ts` (corpus: `transcripts/004-build-plan/`, v2.1.251,
plus its on-disk subagent transcript). Two assumptions in this plan were
contradicted and amended in place: subagent sidechains are separate files on
modern versions (see the §2 correctness-rules table), and the request-start
`user` row is reached via a `parentUuid` walk through `attachment` rows, not
by file adjacency. Also confirmed: `ai-title` payload is
`{ type, aiTitle, sessionId }`, rewritten repeatedly (take the last);
new unrecognized record types already exist (skip-and-count is load-bearing
on day one); several `usage` subfields are optional.
*Acceptance:* types compile; a stub engine returning canned data satisfies
them end-to-end through a stub worker; the pre-freeze log inspection findings
are recorded in the contract's comments.

### WP-03 — Parser ✅ complete (PR #15, 2026-08-30)
**Depends on:** WP-02. **Parallel with:** WP-04, WP-06, WP-09.
Streaming JSONL parser implementing the correctness rules table (dedup,
synthetic exclusion, skip-and-count, version warnings, minimal field surface,
content-poison test) and the validation/security rules (three verdicts,
numeric hygiene, typed-record copying, line-length cap).
Validation uses hand-rolled guards: with a dozen-field surface they are less
code than a schema library. (Zod v4.5 was considered and rejected for this
hot path — a session log is thousands of lines, not enough to need it, and
the dependency buys nothing here. Fine elsewhere in the app if a real need
appears.)
*Acceptance:* unit tests for every rule, plus adversarial tests: malformed
lines, prototype-pollution keys, hostile strings in metadata fields, negative
/ NaN token counts, a single multi-hundred-MB line; parses a 100MB synthetic
file without loading it into one string (that fixture is generated by a
script at test time and git-ignored, never committed).

**Implementation notes (2026-08-30):** `src/engine/parser.ts` (line-fed
`SessionParser` + streaming `parseSession`) over `src/engine/jsonl-stream.ts`
(byte splitter enforcing `MAX_LINE_LENGTH_BYTES` with one line of buffer).
Decisions taken with the user: over-cap lines count as malformed (toward the
reject ratio) *and* get the `line-length-cap-exceeded` warning; structurally
broken assistant rows (no `message.id` / `model` / `usage` object /
`timestamp`) count as malformed, numeric failures as
`invalidUsageRowsSkipped`; metadata strings are stripped of C0/C1 control
characters and clamped, not just clamped; `parseSession` takes an optional
`knownModels` set (the engine passes the pricing config's ids) so the parser
can emit `unknown-models` while staying pricing-blind; the 100MB test runs
on every `npm test` (`scripts/generate-large-fixture.ts` →
`fixtures/generated/`, git-ignored, ~1s). Also: `rejectionReason(parsed)`
derives the `EngineOutcome` reason from `stats`, because the contract's
`ParsedSession` carries no reason field — no contract change; legacy
sidechain recovery indexes `uuid`/`parentUuid` of assistant rows too
(metadata only) and stops at the first non-sidechain ancestor; a request's
completion timestamp is the last content-block row's. Test files and
`scripts/` type-check under a separate `tsconfig.test.json` so Node types
never reach browser code.

### WP-04 — Pricing config and cost engine ✅ complete (PR #15, 2026-08-30)
**Depends on:** WP-02. **Parallel with:** WP-03, WP-06, WP-09.
`pricing.json` populated from the published pricing page (with `pricesAsOf`);
actual-cost computation per request (base, cache read, 5m/1h writes, output,
tier/speed modifiers); unknown-model reporting.
*Acceptance:* hand-computed unit tests (values worked out on paper, not
generated by code) for each modifier combination.

**Implementation notes (2026-08-30):** rates verified against the live
pricing page, not memory (`src/config/pricing.ts` records the provenance of
every multiplier). `priority` is priced at standard: Priority Tier is a
pre-purchased capacity commitment, not a per-token premium. Cache-write
tokens the `cache_creation` split does not cover are priced at 5m (the API
default TTL) rather than dropped. **Known gap:** the 1.1× `inference_geo:
"us"` data-residency multiplier is not modeled because the frozen
`RequestUsage` does not carry `inference_geo` (F5 ignores it) — a candidate
contract amendment (add `inferenceGeo?: string`, price it as a third
multiplier) once WP-06 has a fixture; until then US-only-inference sessions
are understated by 10%.

### WP-05 — Counterfactual simulator ✅ complete (PR #15, 2026-08-30; golden-fixture matching pending WP-06)
**Depends on:** WP-03, WP-04.
The core product: replay the session under each TTL; per-bucket partition;
gap-driven expiry; hard resets; insight-event generation (§3 above).
*Acceptance:* unit tests for reset/expiry/refresh edge cases, plus the golden
fixtures from WP-06 matching to the cent.

**Implementation notes (2026-08-30):** `src/engine/simulator.ts` +
`src/engine/engine.ts` (the real `AnalysisEngine`, now wired into the
worker). The scenario at the *observed* TTL reproduces the log exactly (the
§5 reconciliation property holds by construction); a counterfactual edits
only the requests where the two TTL windows disagree, all-or-nothing:
shortening turns a read after a >5m same-thread gap into a 5m write (the
feasibility §7 rule), and lengthening turns a re-write after a 5m–1h gap
back into a read bounded by what was warm after the previous request. The
lengthening direction is an addition to the feasibility model, which only
covered shortening — without it 1h could never win for a 5m-configured
session. Gaps are measured between request *starts* (F3). Hard resets
(model / effort / version) empty the cache in every scenario and attribute
no expiry to that gap. Only the bucket's dominant-TTL write share is
repriced; server-tool writes keep their TTL as the `server-tool-5m` class
and are not simulated for expiry. **Contract wording note (post-review):**
`contract.ts` says the residual split tokens are the server-tool share, and
in the same paragraph that server tools only add 5m writes so nonzero 1h
tokens are user-controlled. Those conflict for a 5m-dominant bucket with a
1h residual (a mid-session config flip). The simulator follows the
rationale: the server-tool share is only the 5m residual of a 1h-dominant
bucket; in a 5m-dominant bucket every write is user-controlled and repriced
per scenario. The warm entry's observed TTL is the bucket's dominant TTL,
not the previous request's own split (a request whose only write was a
server-tool 5m write must not shorten the user's live 1h entry). Amend the
contract text to match when it is next touched. Unpriced requests are still replayed (so

### WP-06 — Fixtures and golden data
**Depends on:** WP-02 (shapes only). **Parallel with:** WP-03, WP-04.

2. **Real sessions generated by Claude** enacting scenarios (a tight agent

**Bring `prototype-sim.py` to full parity with the §2 correctness-rules

This makes the Python sim an independently written second implementation,
not a trusted oracle: disagreements are settled by hand computation (see §5).
Note (WP-02 inspection): on modern Claude Code versions a "captured subagent

legacy path and stays synthetic.
*Acceptance:* golden files committed; harness wired into `npm test`; includes

expiry-heavy path must be exercised by real data too); real captures are
content-scrubbed by a script (adapt the redaction scripts from this repo's

**Depends on:** nothing (MVP definition in this plan is the brief).

A dedicated **Claude Design** session produces the visual direction and screen

Exports (screens, and the canvas link) are committed to `docs/design/` so

*Acceptance:* every screen and state listed above has a design in

### WP-07 — UI shell
**Depends on:** WP-02; WP-D (visual design).
**Parallel with:** WP-05.
Upload (drag-drop + picker), Web Worker wiring with progress bar and cancel,
in-memory history of this browser session's analyses, "find your logs"

`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set; note the 30-day default cleanup), privacy statement with repo
link, data policy page, sample-session loader. File-size cap and the three

states. Sets up the i18n foundation: locale resource files, the translation

goes through it (English-only catalog for MVP).
*Acceptance:* full flow works against the WP-02 stub engine; cancel actually
terminates the worker mid-parse; a non-session file gets the plain-language

### WP-08 — Results and insights UI
**Depends on:** WP-05, WP-07, WP-D.
Session identification card (title/`cwd`/branch/span/models, with
metadata-only fallback when `ai-title` is absent), recommendation card (with

educational explainers, approximation disclosure (§7 conservatism), skipped

*Acceptance:* renders correctly for each WP-06 sample, including the

1	# Build plan
2	
3	The plan for taking cache-ttl-analyzer from scaffolding to a deployed MVP.
4	Grounded in the research at
5	[docs/design/claude-code-session-logs/feasibility.md](design/claude-code-session-logs/feasibility.md)
6	(referenced below as "the feasibility doc") — read it before implementing the
7	parser or simulator; it documents the traps that make naive implementations
8	silently wrong.
9	
10	This plan is decomposed into **work packages (WPs)** sized for individual Claude
11	sessions, with an explicit dependency graph so independent WPs can run in
12	parallel.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 1. MVP definition
17	
18	A static web app, deployed to Cloudflare, where a user:
19	
20	1. Uploads **one Claude Code session log (JSONL)** at a time — or loads a
21	   bundled sample.
22	2. Watches analysis run **entirely in their browser** (Web Worker), with a
23	   progress indicator and a cancel button.
24	3. Gets a verdict: what the session actually cost at published Anthropic API
25	   rates, what it *would have cost* under the other cache TTL (5m vs 1h), and a
26	   recommendation.
27	4. Sees cache-behavior insights: cache invalidations (expiry gaps, and hard
28	   resets from model / effort / version changes), warm-read counts, and short
29	   educational explanations of each.
30	5. Can revisit sessions analyzed earlier in the same browser session
31	   (in-memory history only — nothing persisted).
32	
33	Plus: clear instructions for finding session logs on macOS and Windows, a
34	prominent privacy statement ("analysis is local; this is open source — verify
35	it yourself" with a link to the repo), a dedicated **data policy page** (see
36	§3a), and a "prices as of" date on every dollar figure.
37	
38	Two cross-cutting requirements, cheap now and expensive to retrofit:
39	
40	- **Localization-ready from day one.** MVP ships English only, but no
41	  user-facing string is hard-coded in a component: all copy lives in locale
42	  resource files (react-i18next or equivalent — chosen in WP-07), and all
43	  number, currency, date, and duration formatting goes through the `Intl`
44	  APIs keyed to the active locale. Adding a second language later must be a
45	  translation task, not a refactor.
46	- **Data policy page**: a first-class page, linked from the footer and the
47	  upload screen, stating in plain language: analysis runs entirely in the
48	  browser; the file is never uploaded, stored, or sent anywhere; the strict
49	  CSP enforces this at the platform level (with a one-line "check devtools"
50	  pointer); no analytics or tracking in the MVP; the project is open source
51	  (repo link); and any future optional API-powered analysis will be opt-in
52	  with an explicit, itemized disclosure of what would be sent.
53	
54	### Non-goals for MVP (deferred, in rough priority order)
55	
56	- **Anthropic API deep-analysis feature** (upload timestamps/token counts for
57	  richer analysis). Deferred until MVP proves useful. When picked up, the
58	  BYO-API-key vs. our-key-plus-rate-limiting decision gets made then.
59	- Multi-file / folder upload and cross-session rollups (requires global dedup
60	  and cross-session cache modeling — feasibility doc §6.3, §7).
61	- Provider-specific rate tables (Bedrock, Vertex). MVP uses Anthropic
62	  published API rates only — see decision log.
63	- Claude Code **web JSON export** input. Unverified that it carries `usage`
64	  (feasibility doc §10). JSONL only for MVP.
65	- Durable persistence, accounts, authentication.
66	- In-app billing-mode questionnaire (feasibility §3 suggests asking the user;
67	  MVP states the API-rates framing as a label instead — see D12).
68	- Hybrid-TTL guidance (1h stable prefix + 5m tail, feasibility §10) — the
69	  logs can't support a computed number, only qualitative advice; revisit
70	  post-MVP.
71	
72	---
73	
74	## 2. Architecture
75	
76	- **Stack:** React + TypeScript + Vite. Deployed as **static assets on
77	  Cloudflare Workers** via Wrangler. **No server-side code in the MVP** — this
78	  is deliberate: the strongest form of the privacy claim is that there is no
79	  backend to send data to.
80	- **Analysis engine** (`src/engine/`): pure TypeScript, zero DOM/React
81	  dependencies, so it runs in a Web Worker and is unit-testable in Node.
82	  - **Parser** reads only the fields it needs (`type`, `timestamp`,
83	    `message.id`, `message.model`, `message.usage`, `isSidechain`, `agentId`,
84	    `effort`, `version`, plus `uuid`/`parentUuid`/`timestamp` of `user` and
85	    `attachment` rows for threading and request-start pairing, and
86	    `sessionId`/`cwd`/`gitBranch` for the identification card) and **never
87	    reads `message.content`** — enforced by a test that
88	    feeds a session whose content blocks are poison values and asserts they
89	    never appear in any output (feasibility doc §9). One deliberate, named
90	    exception: the `ai-title` record (the short session title Claude Code
91	    generates), read for the session identification card (§3) — a single
92	    string, not conversation content. Not every session has one (4 of 7 in
93	    the research corpus); payload shape to be verified in WP-03.
94	  - **Simulator** implements the counterfactual model from the feasibility
95	    doc: see §3 below.
96	- **Web Worker** wraps the engine: streams the file
97	  (`File.stream()` + line splitting, so large logs don't need one giant
98	  string), posts progress messages, and supports cancellation (terminate).
99	- **Pricing config** (`src/config/pricing.json`): per-model base rates, cache
100	  multipliers (read 0.1×, 5m write 1.25×, 1h write 2.0×), `service_tier` and
101	  `speed` modifiers, and a top-level `pricesAsOf` date shown in the UI.
102	  Unknown model IDs are reported to the user, never guessed; degradation
103	  policy: unpriced requests are excluded and disclosed, their share measured
104	  in **total tokens (input + cache + output) across deduped requests**, and
105	  the verdict is suppressed when that share exceeds **10%** (both the metric
106	  and the constant are named in the WP-02 contract so verdicts are
107	  deterministic).
108	- **UI** consumes a frozen engine contract (WP-02) so UI and engine work can
109	  proceed in parallel.
110	- **Logging** goes through a small leveled abstraction (`loglevel`, `tslog`,
111	  or a thin wrapper — chosen in WP-01), used everywhere including the worker
112	  (worker log events forwarded to the main thread). Quiet by default in
113	  production; a debug flag (query param or `localStorage` toggle, documented
114	  on the data policy page) elevates verbosity so users can self-serve
115	  troubleshooting output. **Console-only, never shipped anywhere** — remote
116	  log collection would contradict the CSP/privacy stance. Anything the user
117	  needs to act on (skipped records, warnings) still surfaces in the UI, not
118	  just the log.
119	
120	### Input validation and secure file handling
121	
122	The app is static and client-side, so the threat model is a malicious or
123	corrupted **file** being processed in the user's own browser — plus proving to
124	users that nothing is exfiltrated. Rules:
125	
126	- **Three validation verdicts:** *valid*; *valid with warnings* (skipped
127	  records, out-of-range version, unknown model); or *not a session log* — no
128	  assistant rows carrying `usage`, or malformed lines exceeding **10% of
129	  non-empty lines** (an exact named constant in the WP-02 contract) — with a
130	  plain-language error, never a garbage analysis.
131	- **Numeric hygiene:** every usage field is checked finite and non-negative
132	  before pricing; bad rows are skipped and counted.
133	- **Log-derived strings are untrusted input.** Title, `cwd`, `gitBranch`,
134	  model IDs render only as text nodes (no `innerHTML` anywhere), length-clamped.
135	- **No raw JSON into app state.** The parser copies the needed fields into
136	  typed records and discards the parsed object — no spreading of parsed
137	  objects, which also neutralizes prototype-pollution keys (`__proto__`,
138	  `constructor`).
139	- **Resource limits:** file-size cap with a clear message; streaming parse
140	  with a per-line length cap so one giant line can't exhaust tab memory;
141	  analysis in a worker so the page stays responsive; cancel always available.
142	- **CSP as proof, not just promise:** deploy with a strict
143	  Content-Security-Policy (`default-src 'self'`; no external `connect-src`)
144	  so "your data never leaves the browser" is enforced by the platform and
145	  verifiable in devtools — and mention that in the privacy statement.
146	- **Nothing persisted:** the file is never written to storage; in-memory
147	  history keeps analysis results, not file bytes.
148	
149	### Engine correctness rules (from the feasibility doc — all mandatory)
150	
151	| Rule | Source |
152	|---|---|
153	| Dedup rows on `message.id` (one row per content block, each carries full usage; up to 13× overstatement otherwise) | §6.1 |
154	| Exclude `message.model == "<synthetic>"` rows | §6.2 |
155	| Partition sidechains **per subagent thread**, not as one boolean bucket: each subagent has its own cache namespace. **Amended by the WP-02 inspection (2026-08-30, contract F2):** on v2.1.251 subagent transcripts are *separate files* (`<project>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-<agentId>.jsonl`, rows carrying `agentId` and `isSidechain: true`, `parentUuid` chains self-contained) — not interleaved rows in the main file, which is a legacy-version case. Thread key = `agentId` when present; otherwise the row belongs to the main thread unless `isSidechain` is true, in which case threads are recovered from `parentUuid`-chain roots. Consequence: a modern main-session upload contains **no** subagent traffic; the subagent bucket appears when the uploaded file is itself a subagent transcript or a legacy interleaved log | §6.4 + review + WP-02 inspection |
156	| Hard cache reset on any change of `model`, `effort`, or `version`, independent of elapsed time | §6.6 |
157	| Price per request (models/tiers/speed can vary mid-session); honor `service_tier` and `speed` | §6.5 |
158	| Gap timing: request start = the nearest `user`-row ancestor's timestamp found by walking `parentUuid` (**refined by the WP-02 inspection, contract F3:** the immediate parent is usually an `attachment` row, so the walk must index `uuid`/`parentUuid`/`timestamp` of `user` *and* `attachment` rows — metadata only, never content); fall back to the assistant row's own timestamp when no ancestor resolves | §7 + review + WP-02 inspection |
159	| Expiry model is all-or-nothing per gap; this is conservative toward 5m — disclose it in the UI | §7 |
160	| Effective TTL comes from `usage.cache_creation` (`ephemeral_5m` / `ephemeral_1h` split). Counterfactuals reprice **only the user-controllable share**; server-tool 5m writes stay at 5m in both scenarios and are tracked as their own expiry class. The reconciliation check (§5) replays each request with its **observed per-request split**, not a single session-wide TTL | §2 + review |
161	| Unrecognized record types are skipped and counted, surfaced as "N records skipped" | §4 |
162	| Warn (don't fail) when `version` is outside the validated range | §4 |
163	
164	---
165	
166	## 3. What the analysis reports
167	
168	**First, a session identification card** so the user can confirm they loaded
169	the session they intended — built entirely from content-free metadata: the
170	session title (from the `ai-title` record when present), working directory
171	(`cwd`), git branch, date and time span, duration, request count, model(s),
172	Claude Code version, and file name/size. Message content is never shown; the
173	card is why it never needs to be.
174	
175	**Headline:** the main-conversation bucket. Cost at 5m vs cost at 1h,
176	recommendation, and delta — labelled as *notional cost at published Anthropic
177	API rates* with a one-line rationale (subscription users have no per-token
178	bill; API-rate framing is what an API/Bedrock/credits user pays and what
179	everyone should understand — see decision log).
180	
181	**Conditionally:** if the uploaded file contains sidechain turns — a legacy
182	log with interleaved `isSidechain` rows, or a modern per-subagent transcript
183	from `<session-id>/subagents/` uploaded directly (WP-02 inspection, contract
184	F2) — a second section
185	for the **subagent bucket** (`subagentPromptCacheTtl`), with its own
186	recommendation. When no sidechains exist, this section does not appear, and
187	the tool does not imply it evaluated subagent traffic (feasibility doc §3).
188	
189	**Insights (the educational layer):**
190	
191	- Timeline of cache events: writes, warm reads, expiries (with the gap that
192	  caused each), hard resets (annotated with the cause: model switch, effort
193	  change, version upgrade).
194	- Counts: cache invalidations, warm-read requests, wasted-write tokens.
195	- Observed effective TTL per bucket, and whether the configuration was
196	  provably explicit (the two unambiguous patterns from feasibility doc §3) —
197	  otherwise no claim about defaults.
198	- Session shape summary: request count, span, largest gap, share of gaps in
199	  the 5m–1h band (the only band where the choice matters).
200	- A pointer to Claude Code's built-in live cache stats (`/usage`, v2.1.251+)
201	  for monitoring cache behavior going forward.
202	
203	---
204	
205	## 4. Work packages
206	
207	Sized so each WP is one focused session producing one PR into `main`. Every PR
208	passes CI (typecheck, lint, tests, build) and CodeRabbit review.
209	
210	### WP-01 — Scaffold and tooling ✅ complete (PR #11, 2026-08-30)
211	**Depends on:** nothing. **Blocks:** everything.
212	Vite + React + TS app skeleton; Vitest; Oxlint + Prettier (D14 — was
213	"ESLint + Prettier"); `wrangler.jsonc`
214	for Workers static assets; npm scripts (`dev`, `build`, `test`, `lint`,
215	`typecheck`, `deploy`); the logging abstraction (an in-house ~100-line
216	wrapper was chosen, `src/lib/logger.ts`) with the debug-flag mechanism;
217	README "Development" section filled in.
218	*Acceptance:* `npm run build && npm test` green; `wrangler dev` serves the
219	placeholder app.
220	
221	### WP-02 — Engine contract (do in the same session as WP-01) ✅ complete (PR #11, 2026-08-30)
222	**Depends on:** WP-01. **Blocks:** WP-03, WP-04, WP-05, WP-07, WP-08.
223	The frozen TypeScript interfaces everything else codes against:
224	`ParsedSession` (deduped request records + skip/warning counts),
225	`AnalysisResult` (per-bucket actual/counterfactual costs, recommendation,
226	insight events), the Web Worker message protocol (start / progress / cancel /
227	result / error), and the `pricing.json` schema.
228	
229	**Before freezing, inspect real session logs** to resolve the known unknowns
230	that would otherwise force amendments: the `ai-title` payload shape, the
231	user-row → assistant-row request-start pairing, and sidechain thread
232	identification (`parentUuid`/`uuid` chains) against a real multi-subagent
233	session. The contract must also pin down two semantics the analysis depends
234	on: the **unknown-model degradation policy** (excluded-and-disclosed;
235	verdict suppressed above a threshold) and **mixed-TTL write handling** in
236	counterfactuals (server tools insert their own 5m writes regardless of the
237	user's setting — default model: hold them at 5m in both scenarios as a
238	separate expiry class and reprice only the user-controllable share; WP-02
239	finalizes and documents this so the simulator is deterministic).
240	
241	Documented inline; changes after freeze require touching this plan. The
242	insight-event taxonomy is the one section expected to be amended (WP-08 and
243	WP-D consume it and will discover needs).
244	
245	**Inspection outcome (2026-08-30):** findings F1–F7 are recorded at the top
246	of `src/engine/contract.ts` (corpus: `transcripts/004-build-plan/`, v2.1.251,
247	plus its on-disk subagent transcript). Two assumptions in this plan were
248	contradicted and amended in place: subagent sidechains are separate files on
249	modern versions (see the §2 correctness-rules table), and the request-start
250	`user` row is reached via a `parentUuid` walk through `attachment` rows, not
251	by file adjacency. Also confirmed: `ai-title` payload is
252	`{ type, aiTitle, sessionId }`, rewritten repeatedly (take the last);
253	new unrecognized record types already exist (skip-and-count is load-bearing
254	on day one); several `usage` subfields are optional.
255	*Acceptance:* types compile; a stub engine returning canned data satisfies
256	them end-to-end through a stub worker; the pre-freeze log inspection findings
257	are recorded in the contract's comments.
258	
259	### WP-03 — Parser ✅ complete (PR #15, 2026-08-30)
260	**Depends on:** WP-02. **Parallel with:** WP-04, WP-06, WP-09.
261	Streaming JSONL parser implementing the correctness rules table (dedup,
262	synthetic exclusion, skip-and-count, version warnings, minimal field surface,
263	content-poison test) and the validation/security rules (three verdicts,
264	numeric hygiene, typed-record copying, line-length cap).
265	Validation uses hand-rolled guards: with a dozen-field surface they are less
266	code than a schema library. (Zod v4.5 was considered and rejected for this
267	hot path — a session log is thousands of lines, not enough to need it, and
268	the dependency buys nothing here. Fine elsewhere in the app if a real need
269	appears.)
270	*Acceptance:* unit tests for every rule, plus adversarial tests: malformed
271	lines, prototype-pollution keys, hostile strings in metadata fields, negative
272	/ NaN token counts, a single multi-hundred-MB line; parses a 100MB synthetic
273	file without loading it into one string (that fixture is generated by a
274	script at test time and git-ignored, never committed).
275	
276	**Implementation notes (2026-08-30):** `src/engine/parser.ts` (line-fed
277	`SessionParser` + streaming `parseSession`) over `src/engine/jsonl-stream.ts`
278	(byte splitter enforcing `MAX_LINE_LENGTH_BYTES` with one line of buffer).
279	Decisions taken with the user: over-cap lines count as malformed (toward the
280	reject ratio) *and* get the `line-length-cap-exceeded` warning; structurally
281	broken assistant rows (no `message.id` / `model` / `usage` object /
282	`timestamp`) count as malformed, numeric failures as
283	`invalidUsageRowsSkipped`; metadata strings are stripped of C0/C1 control
284	characters and clamped, not just clamped; `parseSession` takes an optional
285	`knownModels` set (the engine passes the pricing config's ids) so the parser
286	can emit `unknown-models` while staying pricing-blind; the 100MB test runs
287	on every `npm test` (`scripts/generate-large-fixture.ts` →
288	`fixtures/generated/`, git-ignored, ~1s). Also: `rejectionReason(parsed)`
289	derives the `EngineOutcome` reason from `stats`, because the contract's
290	`ParsedSession` carries no reason field — no contract change; legacy
291	sidechain recovery indexes `uuid`/`parentUuid` of assistant rows too
292	(metadata only) and stops at the first non-sidechain ancestor; a request's
293	completion timestamp is the last content-block row's. Test files and
294	`scripts/` type-check under a separate `tsconfig.test.json` so Node types
295	never reach browser code.
296	
297	### WP-04 — Pricing config and cost engine ✅ complete (PR #15, 2026-08-30)
298	**Depends on:** WP-02. **Parallel with:** WP-03, WP-06, WP-09.
299	`pricing.json` populated from the published pricing page (with `pricesAsOf`);
300	actual-cost computation per request (base, cache read, 5m/1h writes, output,
301	tier/speed modifiers); unknown-model reporting.
302	*Acceptance:* hand-computed unit tests (values worked out on paper, not
303	generated by code) for each modifier combination.
304	
305	**Implementation notes (2026-08-30):** rates verified against the live
306	pricing page, not memory (`src/config/pricing.ts` records the provenance of
307	every multiplier). `priority` is priced at standard: Priority Tier is a
308	pre-purchased capacity commitment, not a per-token premium. Cache-write
309	tokens the `cache_creation` split does not cover are priced at 5m (the API
310	default TTL) rather than dropped. **Known gap:** the 1.1× `inference_geo:
311	"us"` data-residency multiplier is not modeled because the frozen
312	`RequestUsage` does not carry `inference_geo` (F5 ignores it) — a candidate
313	contract amendment (add `inferenceGeo?: string`, price it as a third
314	multiplier) once WP-06 has a fixture; until then US-only-inference sessions
315	are understated by 10%.
316	
317	### WP-05 — Counterfactual simulator ✅ complete (PR #15, 2026-08-30; golden-fixture matching pending WP-06)
318	**Depends on:** WP-03, WP-04.
319	The core product: replay the session under each TTL; per-bucket partition;
320	gap-driven expiry; hard resets; insight-event generation (§3 above).
321	*Acceptance:* unit tests for reset/expiry/refresh edge cases, plus the golden
322	fixtures from WP-06 matching to the cent.
323	
324	**Implementation notes (2026-08-30):** `src/engine/simulator.ts` +
325	`src/engine/engine.ts` (the real `AnalysisEngine`, now wired into the
326	worker). The scenario at the *observed* TTL reproduces the log exactly (the
327	§5 reconciliation property holds by construction); a counterfactual edits
328	only the requests where the two TTL windows disagree, all-or-nothing:
329	shortening turns a read after a >5m same-thread gap into a 5m write (the
330	feasibility §7 rule), and lengthening turns a re-write after a 5m–1h gap
331	back into a read bounded by what was warm after the previous request. The
332	lengthening direction is an addition to the feasibility model, which only
333	covered shortening — without it 1h could never win for a 5m-configured
334	session. Gaps are measured between request *starts* (F3). Hard resets
335	(model / effort / version) empty the cache in every scenario and attribute
336	no expiry to that gap. Only the bucket's dominant-TTL write share is
337	repriced; server-tool writes keep their TTL as the `server-tool-5m` class
338	and are not simulated for expiry. **Contract wording note (post-review):**
339	`contract.ts` says the residual split tokens are the server-tool share, and
340	in the same paragraph that server tools only add 5m writes so nonzero 1h
341	tokens are user-controlled. Those conflict for a 5m-dominant bucket with a
342	1h residual (a mid-session config flip). The simulator follows the
343	rationale: the server-tool share is only the 5m residual of a 1h-dominant
344	bucket; in a 5m-dominant bucket every write is user-controlled and repriced
345	per scenario. The warm entry's observed TTL is the bucket's dominant TTL,
346	not the previous request's own split (a request whose only write was a
347	server-tool 5m write must not shorten the user's live 1h entry). Amend the
348	contract text to match when it is next touched. Unpriced requests are still replayed (so
349	events and cache state stay right) but excluded from dollars. An exact cost
350	tie recommends the observed TTL. A subagent-only upload still yields an
351	empty `main` bucket with `no-verdict`. Hand-computed tests at Opus 5 rates
352	plus a reconciliation run over the real v2.1.251 corpus; the WP-06 golden
353	harness is the remaining acceptance item.
354	
355	### WP-06 — Fixtures and golden data
356	**Depends on:** WP-02 (shapes only). **Parallel with:** WP-03, WP-04.
357	Two kinds of fixtures:
358	1. **Crafted synthetic JSONL** exercising each trap: content-block
359	   duplication, synthetic rows, sidechains (including parallel subagents
360	   with interleaved rows), mid-session model switch, effort
361	   change, version change, gaps in the 5m–1h band, mixed
362	   `ephemeral_5m`/`ephemeral_1h` writes, unknown record types, unknown model —
363	   plus adversarial fixtures: a non-session JSONL, malformed lines, hostile
364	   metadata strings, prototype-pollution keys, invalid numerics.
365	2. **Real sessions generated by Claude** enacting scenarios (a tight agent
366	   loop where 5m wins; a long gap-heavy session where 1h wins; a session that
367	   switches models mid-way) — these double as the bundled samples in
368	   `public/samples/` and as end-to-end verification that the tool's verdicts
369	   match intuition.
370	
371	**Bring `prototype-sim.py` to full parity with the §2 correctness-rules
372	table first** — as written it implements almost none of it (no sidechain
373	partition, no hard resets on model/effort/version, no `service_tier`/`speed`
374	modifiers, gap timing from the wrong timestamp, unknown models silently
375	priced as Opus, stale price table) — verified by its own hand-computed
376	tests. Only then have it emit expected-output JSON per fixture; commit those
377	as golden files with a test harness that runs the TS engine against them.
378	This makes the Python sim an independently written second implementation,
379	not a trusted oracle: disagreements are settled by hand computation (see §5).
380	Note (WP-02 inspection): on modern Claude Code versions a "captured subagent
381	session" is a set of files — the main `<session-id>.jsonl` plus
382	`<session-id>/subagents/agent-<agentId>.jsonl` per subagent (parallel
383	subagents = multiple files); the interleaved-row fixture exercises the
384	legacy path and stays synthetic.
385	*Acceptance:* golden files committed; harness wired into `npm test`; includes
386	a **captured real subagent session (with parallel subagents)** and a
387	**captured 5m-configured session** (every corpus session ran at 1h — the
388	expiry-heavy path must be exercised by real data too); real captures are
389	content-scrubbed by a script (adapt the redaction scripts from this repo's
390	`publish-transcript` skill) since they ship publicly.
391	
392	### WP-D — UX design (Claude Design session)
393	**Depends on:** nothing (MVP definition in this plan is the brief).
394	**Parallel with:** WP-03, WP-04, WP-06, WP-09.
395	A dedicated **Claude Design** session produces the visual direction and screen
396	designs for the whole flow: landing page (privacy statement, upload,
397	"find your logs" instructions, samples), the analyzing state (progress +
398	cancel), and the results view (session identification card, recommendation
399	card, cost comparison,
400	conditional subagent section, cache-event timeline, educational explainers,
401	session-history strip). It should also cover the empty/error states: unknown
402	model, skipped records, version warning, malformed file. Include the data
403	policy page, and design copy areas with text expansion in mind (translated
404	strings run ~30% longer than English). **Constraint from the strict CSP:**
405	no external assets — fonts are self-hosted or system stacks, no external
406	webfonts, CDN images, or third-party embeds; a design that depends on them
407	would force weakening the privacy-proving CSP.
408	Exports (screens, and the canvas link) are committed to `docs/design/` so
409	WP-07 and WP-08 sessions can implement against them without guessing.
410	*Acceptance:* every screen and state listed above has a design in
411	`docs/design/`; user has signed off on the direction.
412	
413	### WP-07 — UI shell
414	**Depends on:** WP-02; WP-D (visual design).
415	**Parallel with:** WP-05.
416	Upload (drag-drop + picker), Web Worker wiring with progress bar and cancel,
417	in-memory history of this browser session's analyses, "find your logs"
418	instructions (macOS: `~/.claude/projects/<project-slug>/<session-id>.jsonl`;
419	Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\projects\...`; subagent transcripts beside
420	the session file in `<session-id>/subagents/`; both roots moved by
421	`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set; note the 30-day default cleanup), privacy statement with repo
422	link, data policy page, sample-session loader. File-size cap and the three
423	validation verdicts (valid / warnings / not a session log) as distinct UI
424	states. Sets up the i18n foundation: locale resource files, the translation
425	hook pattern, and `Intl`-based formatters — every string in WP-07 and WP-08
426	goes through it (English-only catalog for MVP).
427	*Acceptance:* full flow works against the WP-02 stub engine; cancel actually
428	terminates the worker mid-parse; a non-session file gets the plain-language
429	rejection, not a broken analysis.
430	
431	### WP-08 — Results and insights UI
432	**Depends on:** WP-05, WP-07, WP-D.
433	Session identification card (title/`cwd`/branch/span/models, with
434	metadata-only fallback when `ai-title` is absent), recommendation card (with
435	the API-rates framing line and `pricesAsOf` date), cost comparison, conditional subagent section, cache-event timeline,
436	educational explainers, approximation disclosure (§7 conservatism), skipped
437	records / version warnings surfaced. When the upload contains no sidechain
438	traffic — every modern main-session upload (F2) — say so explicitly rather
439	than silently omitting the subagent section: the tool evaluated
440	`promptCacheTtl` only, and the subagent transcripts live in
441	`<session-id>/subagents/` if the user wants those analyzed (the engine
442	already yields an empty subagent bucket / `isSidechain` per request to
443	derive this from).
444	*Acceptance:* renders correctly for each WP-06 sample, including the
445	no-sidechain and unknown-model cases.
446	
447	### WP-09 — CI/CD ✅ complete (PR #13, 2026-08-30)
448	**Depends on:** WP-01. **Parallel with:** WP-03, WP-04, WP-06.
449	GitHub Actions owns the whole pipeline (see D15, revised 2026-08-30): one
450	`ci.yml` whose `check` job runs format check, lint, typecheck, test and build
451	on every PR and on `main`, and which uploads `dist/` as an artifact so the
452	deploy jobs ship the exact bytes CI checked rather than rebuilding.
453	Deploys on push to `main` run `wrangler deploy` against a scoped Cloudflare
454	API token held in GitHub Actions secrets.
455	**PR preview deployments** run `wrangler versions upload --preview-alias
456	<branch>`, which publishes a version without touching the live deployment and
457	yields two links — a per-commit preview URL and a stable branch-alias URL that
458	always points at the branch's latest version. A workflow step posts (and
459	updates in place) a single PR comment carrying both, so platform behavior
460	(CSP headers, `File.stream()` in the worker, SPA routing) is verified in the
461	real Workers runtime before merge.
462	Previews build only for branches in this repo — fork PRs cannot read the
463	secrets and must not be handed the token — and preview URLs are public, which
464	is acceptable for a static, open-source app. Document the token setup in
465	README. Branch protection on `main`. Serve the strict CSP and security headers
466	(via the Workers static-assets `_headers` config). ~~Attach
467	**cacheanalyzer.com** as a custom domain on the Worker~~ — done 2026-08-30,
468	ahead of this WP (see D8; `wrangler.jsonc` carries the `routes` custom-domain
469	config).
470	*Acceptance:* a PR shows the checks and gets a preview-URL comment; a merge to
471	`main` deploys, reachable at `workers.dev` and at cacheanalyzer.com (already
472	live); the README's Live URL is updated.
473	
474	**Delivered (PR #13):** `ci.yml` with the `check`/`preview`/`deploy` jobs,
475	`public/_headers`, `.nvmrc` pinning Node 26, and branch protection on `main`
476	(PR required, `check` required to pass). Preview aliases are keyed
477	`pr-<number>-<branch>` rather than branch alone, because normalizing a branch
478	name is not injective (`feat/a` and `feat_a` collapse together, and long
479	branches collide once truncated to the 44-character limit) and an alias binds
480	to whichever version uploaded last.
481	Verified: CI green on #13; both preview URLs served HTTP 200 from the
482	Cloudflare edge with the full CSP and `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`; the app loaded
483	from the preview and its module Web Worker ran to completion with zero CSP
484	violations; the PR comment updated in place across three preview runs instead
485	of duplicating.
486	**Production deploy verified (2026-08-30, merge of #13):** the open question was
487	`wrangler deploy` reconciling the `cacheanalyzer.com` custom-domain route, which
488	previews never exercise (`versions upload` does not touch routes). It succeeded
489	on the first run, so the **Edit Cloudflare Workers** token scope is right.
490	cacheanalyzer.com now serves all eight security headers including the full CSP,
491	and carries no `X-Robots-Tag` — that rule is correctly scoped to preview
492	hostnames only, leaving production indexable.
493	
494	### WP-10 — Launch polish
495	**Depends on:** WP-08, WP-09.
496	README rewrite for end users; verify samples load on the deployed site;
497	cross-browser pass (Chrome plus at least one of Safari/Firefox — the real
498	compatibility risk is `File.stream()` in workers; Edge is Chromium); perf
499	sanity check with the generated 100MB fixture; final wording pass on privacy
500	and approximation disclosures.
501	
502	### Dependency graph
503	
504	```mermaid
505	graph LR
506	    WP01[WP-01 Scaffold] --> WP02[WP-02 Contract]
507	    WP01 --> WP09[WP-09 CI/CD]
508	    WP02 --> WP03[WP-03 Parser]
509	    WP02 --> WP04[WP-04 Pricing]
510	    WP02 --> WP06[WP-06 Fixtures]
511	    WP02 --> WP07[WP-07 UI shell]
512	    WP03 --> WP05[WP-05 Simulator]
513	    WP04 --> WP05
514	    WP06 --> WP05
515	    WP05 --> WP08[WP-08 Results UI]
516	    WP07 --> WP08
517	    WP08 --> WP10[WP-10 Launch]
518	    WP09 --> WP10
519	    WPD([WP-D Claude Design]) --> WP07
520	    WPD --> WP08
521	```
522	
523	**Suggested waves:** ① WP-01+02 (one session) → ② WP-03, WP-04, WP-06, WP-09,
524	and WP-D (the Claude Design session), all in parallel → ③ WP-05 and WP-07 in
525	parallel → ④ WP-08 → ⑤ WP-10.
526	
527	---
528	
529	## 5. Testing strategy
530	
531	- **Unit tests** (Vitest) on parser rules and pricing math, with
532	  hand-computed expected values.
533	- **Golden-fixture cross-validation:** the spec-parity Python simulator
534	  (WP-06) is an independently written second implementation; the TS engine
535	  must reproduce its outputs to the cent on every fixture. Neither
536	  implementation is the oracle — hand-computed tests are the tiebreaker, so
537	  a shared logic bug can't hide in both.
538	- **Actual-vs-simulated reconciliation:** the actual cost is computed exactly
539	  from observed usage; running the simulator at the *observed* TTL must
540	  reproduce it (within the stated approximation) on every fixture — a free
541	  sanity check on the whole simulator.
542	- **Content-poison test:** proves `message.content` never influences or leaks
543	  into output.
544	- **Format-drift canary:** fixtures are tagged with the Claude Code `version`
545	  they represent; the parser's validated-version range lives in one constant,
546	  and CI fails if a golden fixture's version falls outside it. One
547	  deliberately out-of-range fixture is **exempt from the canary** and instead
548	  asserts the warn-don't-fail path, so the two rules never conflict.
549	
550	---
551	
552	## 6. Decision log
553	
554	| # | Decision | Rationale |
555	|---|---|---|
556	| D1 | Anthropic API feature deferred to post-MVP | Keeps MVP fully static: no backend, no rate limiting, strongest privacy story. (User, 2026-08-30) |
557	| D2 | All dollar figures at published Anthropic API rates, clearly labelled | API rates are what usage-billed users pay and what everyone should understand; rationale stated in README and UI. Provider tables (Bedrock/Vertex) deferred. (User) |
558	| D3 | One session upload at a time; in-memory history only | Processing time unknown; persistence deferred until the tool proves useful. (User) |
559	| D4 | Always partition sidechains in the simulation; headline the main bucket; show a subagent section only when the session contains sidechain turns | Partitioning is required for correctness regardless (§6.4); conditional display gives two-bucket value without confusing the majority whose sessions have no subagents. (Claude's vote, accepted) |
560	| D5 | Rates live in a committed `pricing.json` with a `pricesAsOf` date; unknown models reported to the user | Simple, auditable, no runtime fetch. API-driven rates possible later. (User) |
561	| D6 | Fixtures are synthetic + Claude-generated scenario sessions; no personal sessions bundled | Avoids publishing usage patterns; scenarios can be engineered to teach specific lessons and to verify verdicts. (User) |
562	| D7 | The Python simulator — brought to full spec parity in WP-06 — is an **independently written second implementation** generating golden fixtures the TS engine must match; hand-computed tests are the tiebreaker | Re-scoped after independent review: the original prototype implements almost none of the correctness rules and was never a valid oracle. Cross-validation still catches divergent bugs. (Claude's vote, revised) |
563	| D8 | Domain is **cacheanalyzer.com** (purchased 2026-08-30, in the same Cloudflare account the Worker deploys to). Attached as a custom domain on the Worker on 2026-08-30, ahead of WP-09; `workers.dev` and preview URLs stay enabled alongside it | Name was available; buying via Cloudflare Registrar keeps DNS in the same account as the Worker, so Cloudflare manages DNS/TLS automatically. (User) |
564	| D9 | JSONL input only for MVP | Web-export JSON unverified for `usage` data (feasibility §10). |
565	| D10 | Localization-ready architecture from day one; English-only catalog for MVP | Externalized strings + `Intl` formatting are cheap now and a painful retrofit; future languages become translation tasks. (User, 2026-08-30) |
566	| D11 | Dedicated data policy page in the MVP | Data privacy is a core product value; the policy also pre-commits the disclosure standard for any future opt-in API feature. (User, 2026-08-30) |
567	| D12 | No in-app billing-mode questionnaire; the API-rates framing is a stated label | Deliberate simplification of feasibility §3's "ask the user, don't guess"; revisit if users report confusion. (Post-review, 2026-08-30) |
568	| D13 | All logging through a leveled abstraction with a user-accessible debug flag; console-only, no remote collection | Troubleshooting a client-only app depends on users' consoles; remote logging would contradict the privacy stance. (User, 2026-08-30) |
569	| D14 | Oxlint (+ Prettier for formatting) instead of ESLint | Better fit for a Vite + React + TS app: it is Vite's current template default, fast, and needs no plugin stack for the rules we use. (User, 2026-08-30) |
570	| D15 | ~~Deploys via Cloudflare Workers Builds, not a GitHub-stored API token~~ **Revised 2026-08-30 (WP-09):** deploys and PR previews run from GitHub Actions via `wrangler`, authenticated by a scoped Cloudflare API token in GitHub Actions secrets | Originally chosen because the user wanted OIDC/trusted publishing and Cloudflare doesn't support it for `wrangler` deploys ([open feature request](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/discussions/11434)), making Workers Builds the closest no-stored-secret equivalent. Revised when WP-09 was built: keeping every gate in one GitHub Actions run makes ordering explicit (deploy the artifact CI checked, never a rebuild) and keeps CI config reviewable in-repo rather than split across a dashboard. The cost is a stored credential — mitigated by scoping the token to this one account and the `cacheanalyzer.com` zone, and it is revocable from the dashboard. The token comes from Cloudflare's **Edit Cloudflare Workers** template rather than a bare `Workers Scripts: Edit`: `wrangler.jsonc` declares `cacheanalyzer.com` as a custom-domain route, and reconciling that route on deploy also needs zone-level `Workers Routes: Edit`. Still revisit if Cloudflare ships OIDC. (User, 2026-08-30) |
571	| D16 | No post-deploy smoke check asserting security headers against the live site | WP-09 originally required one so a misconfigured `_headers` file would fail the deploy. Judged disproportionate for a project this size: `_headers` is a static file reviewed in the PR diff, and the CSP was verified end-to-end against the real Workers runtime (`wrangler dev`, module worker spawned, zero violations) when it was written. Revisit if the header config starts changing often. (User, 2026-08-30) |
572	
573	## 7. Risks
574	
575	| Risk | Mitigation |
576	|---|---|
577	| Log format is officially internal and unstable (feasibility §4) | Minimal field surface; version pinning + warning; skip-and-count; versioned fixtures in CI |
578	| Pricing goes stale | `pricesAsOf` shown to users; single-file update path; periodic check noted in README |
579	| Counterfactual is approximate (all-or-nothing expiry, feasibility §7) | Conservative direction (understates 1h's downside cases toward 5m) disclosed in the UI |
580	| Subagent path untested against real data | WP-06 must include a real subagent session fixture before WP-05 is called done |
581	| Huge session files stall the browser | Streaming parse in a worker; progress + cancel; 100MB perf test in WP-10 |
582	| Malicious or corrupted uploads (hostile strings, pollution keys, giant lines, non-session files) | Validation verdicts; text-node-only rendering; typed-record copying; size/line caps; adversarial fixtures in WP-03/WP-06; strict CSP |

# Build plan

The plan for taking cache-ttl-analyzer from scaffolding to a deployed MVP.
Grounded in the research at
[docs/design/claude-code-session-logs/feasibility.md](design/claude-code-session-logs/feasibility.md)
(referenced below as "the feasibility doc") — read it before implementing the
parser or simulator; it documents the traps that make naive implementations
silently wrong.

This plan is decomposed into **work packages (WPs)** sized for individual Claude
sessions, with an explicit dependency graph so independent WPs can run in
parallel.

---

## 1. MVP definition

A static web app, deployed to Cloudflare, where a user:

1. Uploads **one Claude Code session log (JSONL)** at a time — or loads a
   bundled sample.
2. Watches analysis run **entirely in their browser** (Web Worker), with a
   progress indicator and a cancel button.
3. Gets a verdict: what the session actually cost at published Anthropic API
   rates, what it *would have cost* under the other cache TTL (5m vs 1h), and a
   recommendation.
4. Sees cache-behavior insights: cache invalidations (expiry gaps, and hard
   resets from model / effort / version changes), warm-read counts, and short
   educational explanations of each.
5. Can revisit sessions analyzed earlier in the same browser session
   (in-memory history only — nothing persisted).

Plus: clear instructions for finding session logs on macOS and Windows, a
prominent privacy statement ("analysis is local; this is open source — verify
it yourself" with a link to the repo), a dedicated **data policy page** (see
§3a), and a "prices as of" date on every dollar figure.

Two cross-cutting requirements, cheap now and expensive to retrofit:

- **Localization-ready from day one.** MVP ships English only, but no
  user-facing string is hard-coded in a component: all copy lives in locale
  resource files (react-i18next or equivalent — chosen in WP-07), and all
  number, currency, date, and duration formatting goes through the `Intl`
  APIs keyed to the active locale. Adding a second language later must be a
  translation task, not a refactor.
- **Data policy page**: a first-class page, linked from the footer and the
  upload screen, stating in plain language: analysis runs entirely in the
  browser; the file is never uploaded, stored, or sent anywhere; the strict
  CSP enforces this at the platform level (with a one-line "check devtools"
  pointer); no analytics or tracking in the MVP; the project is open source
  (repo link); and any future optional API-powered analysis will be opt-in
  with an explicit, itemized disclosure of what would be sent.

### Non-goals for MVP (deferred, in rough priority order)

- **Anthropic API deep-analysis feature** (upload timestamps/token counts for
  richer analysis). Deferred until MVP proves useful. When picked up, the
  BYO-API-key vs. our-key-plus-rate-limiting decision gets made then.
- Multi-file / folder upload and cross-session rollups (requires global dedup
  and cross-session cache modeling — feasibility doc §6.3, §7).
- Provider-specific rate tables (Bedrock, Vertex). MVP uses Anthropic
  published API rates only — see decision log.
- Claude Code **web JSON export** input. Unverified that it carries `usage`
  (feasibility doc §10). JSONL only for MVP.
- Durable persistence, accounts, authentication.
- In-app billing-mode questionnaire (feasibility §3 suggests asking the user;
  MVP states the API-rates framing as a label instead — see D12).
- Hybrid-TTL guidance (1h stable prefix + 5m tail, feasibility §10) — the
  logs can't support a computed number, only qualitative advice; revisit
  post-MVP.

---

## 2. Architecture

- **Stack:** React + TypeScript + Vite. Deployed as **static assets on
  Cloudflare Workers** via Wrangler. **No server-side code in the MVP** — this
  is deliberate: the strongest form of the privacy claim is that there is no
  backend to send data to.
- **Analysis engine** (`src/engine/`): pure TypeScript, zero DOM/React
  dependencies, so it runs in a Web Worker and is unit-testable in Node.
  - **Parser** reads only the fields it needs (`type`, `timestamp`,
    `message.id`, `message.model`, `message.usage`, `isSidechain`, `agentId`,
    `effort`, `version`, plus `uuid`/`parentUuid`/`timestamp` of `user` and
    `attachment` rows for threading and request-start pairing, and
    `sessionId`/`cwd`/`gitBranch` for the identification card) and **never
    reads `message.content`** — enforced by a test that
    feeds a session whose content blocks are poison values and asserts they
    never appear in any output (feasibility doc §9). One deliberate, named
    exception: the `ai-title` record (the short session title Claude Code
    generates), read for the session identification card (§3) — a single
    string, not conversation content. Not every session has one (4 of 7 in
    the research corpus); payload shape to be verified in WP-03.
  - **Simulator** implements the counterfactual model from the feasibility
    doc: see §3 below.
- **Web Worker** wraps the engine: streams the file
  (`File.stream()` + line splitting, so large logs don't need one giant
  string), posts progress messages, and supports cancellation (terminate).
- **Pricing config** (`src/config/pricing.json`): per-model base rates, cache
  multipliers (read 0.1×, 5m write 1.25×, 1h write 2.0×), `service_tier` and
  `speed` modifiers, and a top-level `pricesAsOf` date shown in the UI.
  Unknown model IDs are reported to the user, never guessed; degradation
  policy: unpriced requests are excluded and disclosed, their share measured
  in **total tokens (input + cache + output) across deduped requests**, and
  the verdict is suppressed when that share exceeds **10%** (both the metric
  and the constant are named in the WP-02 contract so verdicts are
  deterministic).
- **UI** consumes a frozen engine contract (WP-02) so UI and engine work can
  proceed in parallel.
- **Logging** goes through a small leveled abstraction (`loglevel`, `tslog`,
  or a thin wrapper — chosen in WP-01), used everywhere including the worker
  (worker log events forwarded to the main thread). Quiet by default in
  production; a debug flag (query param or `localStorage` toggle, documented
  on the data policy page) elevates verbosity so users can self-serve
  troubleshooting output. **Console-only, never shipped anywhere** — remote
  log collection would contradict the CSP/privacy stance. Anything the user
  needs to act on (skipped records, warnings) still surfaces in the UI, not
  just the log.

### Input validation and secure file handling

The app is static and client-side, so the threat model is a malicious or
corrupted **file** being processed in the user's own browser — plus proving to
users that nothing is exfiltrated. Rules:

- **Three validation verdicts:** *valid*; *valid with warnings* (skipped
  records, out-of-range version, unknown model); or *not a session log* — no
  assistant rows carrying `usage`, or malformed lines exceeding **10% of
  non-empty lines** (an exact named constant in the WP-02 contract) — with a
  plain-language error, never a garbage analysis.
- **Numeric hygiene:** every usage field is checked finite and non-negative
  before pricing; bad rows are skipped and counted.
- **Log-derived strings are untrusted input.** Title, `cwd`, `gitBranch`,
  model IDs render only as text nodes (no `innerHTML` anywhere), length-clamped.
- **No raw JSON into app state.** The parser copies the needed fields into
  typed records and discards the parsed object — no spreading of parsed
  objects, which also neutralizes prototype-pollution keys (`__proto__`,
  `constructor`).
- **Resource limits:** file-size cap with a clear message; streaming parse
  with a per-line length cap so one giant line can't exhaust tab memory;
  analysis in a worker so the page stays responsive; cancel always available.
- **CSP as proof, not just promise:** deploy with a strict
  Content-Security-Policy (`default-src 'self'`; no external `connect-src`)
  so "your data never leaves the browser" is enforced by the platform and
  verifiable in devtools — and mention that in the privacy statement.
- **Nothing persisted:** the file is never written to storage; in-memory
  history keeps analysis results, not file bytes.

### Engine correctness rules (from the feasibility doc — all mandatory)

| Rule | Source |
|---|---|
| Dedup rows on `message.id` (one row per content block, each carries full usage; up to 13× overstatement otherwise) | §6.1 |
| Exclude `message.model == "<synthetic>"` rows | §6.2 |
| Partition sidechains **per subagent thread**, not as one boolean bucket: each subagent has its own cache namespace. **Amended by the WP-02 inspection (2026-08-30, contract F2):** on v2.1.251 subagent transcripts are *separate files* (`<project>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-<agentId>.jsonl`, rows carrying `agentId` and `isSidechain: true`, `parentUuid` chains self-contained) — not interleaved rows in the main file, which is a legacy-version case. Thread key = `agentId` when present; otherwise the row belongs to the main thread unless `isSidechain` is true, in which case threads are recovered from `parentUuid`-chain roots. Consequence: a modern main-session upload contains **no** subagent traffic; the subagent bucket appears when the uploaded file is itself a subagent transcript or a legacy interleaved log | §6.4 + review + WP-02 inspection |
| Hard cache reset on any change of `model`, `effort`, or `version`, independent of elapsed time | §6.6 |
| Price per request (models/tiers/speed can vary mid-session); honor `service_tier` and `speed` | §6.5 |
| Gap timing: request start = the nearest `user`-row ancestor's timestamp found by walking `parentUuid` (**refined by the WP-02 inspection, contract F3:** the immediate parent is usually an `attachment` row, so the walk must index `uuid`/`parentUuid`/`timestamp` of `user` *and* `attachment` rows — metadata only, never content); fall back to the assistant row's own timestamp when no ancestor resolves | §7 + review + WP-02 inspection |
| Expiry model is all-or-nothing per gap; this is conservative toward 5m — disclose it in the UI | §7 |
| Effective TTL comes from `usage.cache_creation` (`ephemeral_5m` / `ephemeral_1h` split). Counterfactuals reprice **only the user-controllable share**; server-tool 5m writes stay at 5m in both scenarios and are tracked as their own expiry class. The reconciliation check (§5) replays each request with its **observed per-request split**, not a single session-wide TTL | §2 + review |
| Unrecognized record types are skipped and counted, surfaced as "N records skipped" | §4 |
| Warn (don't fail) when `version` is outside the validated range | §4 |

## 3. What the analysis reports

**First, a session identification card** so the user can confirm they loaded
the session they intended — built entirely from content-free metadata: the
session title (from the `ai-title` record when present), working directory
(`cwd`), git branch, date and time span, duration, request count, model(s),
Claude Code version, and file name/size. Message content is never shown; the
card is why it never needs to be.

**Headline:** the main-conversation bucket. Cost at 5m vs cost at 1h,
recommendation, and delta — labelled as *notional cost at published Anthropic
API rates* with a one-line rationale (subscription users have no per-token
bill; API-rate framing is what an API/Bedrock/credits user pays and what
everyone should understand — see decision log).

**Conditionally:** if the uploaded file contains sidechain turns — a legacy
log with interleaved `isSidechain` rows, or a modern per-subagent transcript
from `<session-id>/subagents/` uploaded directly (WP-02 inspection, contract
F2) — a second section
for the **subagent bucket** (`subagentPromptCacheTtl`), with its own
recommendation. When no sidechains exist, this section does not appear, and
the tool does not imply it evaluated subagent traffic (feasibility doc §3).

**Insights (the educational layer):**

- Timeline of cache events: writes, warm reads, expiries (with the gap that
  caused each), hard resets (annotated with the cause: model switch, effort
  change, version upgrade).
- Counts: cache invalidations, warm-read requests, wasted-write tokens.
- Observed effective TTL per bucket, and whether the configuration was
  provably explicit (the two unambiguous patterns from feasibility doc §3) —
  otherwise no claim about defaults.
- Session shape summary: request count, span, largest gap, share of gaps in
  the 5m–1h band (the only band where the choice matters).
- A pointer to Claude Code's built-in live cache stats (`/usage`, v2.1.251+)
  for monitoring cache behavior going forward.
